source: a bmx game but you have to do an obby to gain speed

answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the BMX park read as a sunny stylized dirt-jump park, or grimy urban concrete?
answers.answer: Make it a sunny stylized dirt-jump park; that is the simplest, clearest fit for the BMX gameplay.

answers.ask: Does the BMX section end at a finish line you race to, or is it a freestyle area you ride around?
answers.answer: Use a finish line the player races to after completing the obby and building speed.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] theme — Q: No theme was stated - should the BMX park read as a sunny stylized dirt-jump park, or grimy urban concrete? A: Make it a sunny stylized dirt-jump park; that is the simplest, clearest fit for the BMX gameplay.
- [author] goal — Q: Does the BMX section end at a finish line you race to, or is it a freestyle area you ride around? A: Use a finish line the player races to after completing the obby and building speed.
- [agent_inferred] obby traversal — Q: Is the speed-building obby completed on foot or while riding the BMX? A: Keep the player on the BMX and make the obby a continuous rideable dirt-jump section so it connects directly into the race.

## Enriched image prompt
Build a sunny stylized BMX dirt-jump park as one point-to-point course. Begin at a clear start line, then lead the rider through a compact speed-building obby made from a continuous dirt roadway with rideable ramps, rollers, banked turns, and jump obstacles. After the obstacle section, open into a faster final straight or broad dirt corridor that carries momentum to a prominent finish line. Surround the course with bright grass and simple cheerful park scenery, keeping the full route readable and every transition wide enough for a BMX bicycle.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Racing because the player controls speed along a finite route ending at a finish line. Obby & Platformer is secondary because an obstacle section precedes the final race.

## Shape and preset
Use `route-point-to-point`, Path (Point to Point): the BMX course starts in one place and ends at the finish. The matching preset is Obstacle Race, adapted for a rideable dirt obby.

## Config requirements
Use `path-road-vehicle` for the continuous BMX-width dirt roadway, `obstacle-jump` for ramps, rollers, and jump gaps, `lane-corridor` for readable painted or packed-earth course edges, `startpoint-line` in both streams for the launch line, and `trigger-finish` in both streams for the terminal finish gate.

## Layout requirements
Place one `startpoint-line` StartPoint at the beginning, one `checkpoint-respawn` recovery marker after the obstacle section with BMX position and orientation aligned down-course, and one `trigger-finish` TriggerZone at the exact far end. No lap trigger is needed because this is point-to-point.

## Layout components
One connected course has two subordinate zones on the same map: a speed-building dirt obby and a faster finishing run. A start line feeds the obstacle roadway, the checkpoint sits at the transition, and the final corridor terminates at the finish gate. Grass and simple park edges enclose the route.

## Render order
Use `authored_plan`: the supported point-to-point racing route must be generated first so every BMX segment connects cleanly, then dressed as a dirt-jump park.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use medium scale because ramps, bike-width corridors, checkpoint, and finish must remain legible across one compact course. The theme is sunny stylized dirt-jump park with bright grass. `P6` is required because the BMX route and obstacle transitions must be valid by construction.
